correctness.rationale: Conditional independence gives an exact q_x(A_t)q_y(A_ct) expectation. Reflection/CLT yields q_x(a)~x sqrt(2/(pi a)); the rate law yields joint alpha-stable operational clocks with b_t=t^(1/alpha)tau^(1-1/alpha). Mellin negative-moment bounds justify the expectation limit. A two-variable Mellin reduction gives the angular integral, monotone covariance proves strict R>1, stable independent increments give R->1, and a tangent half-angle integration yields R_(1/2)(2)=4/3. The standalone checker passed. Fixed c and time asymptotics only.

value.rationale: Joint survival at two *distinct* observation horizons is an operationally natural sequential-reliability observable in a fluctuating transport environment. The exact c-dependent kernel measures how rate sharing enhances simultaneous persistence and how it decorrelates as observation times separate; the double-time 4/3 constant is new information beyond the already known equal-time pi/2. The result is exact, reproducible, and not a mere numerical retabling or parameter substitution.
